name: CodeRAG-Bench: Can Retrieval Augment Code Generation?
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: NAACL 2025 (arXiv preprint June 2024, v2 Feb 2025; published NAACL 2025 Findings, pages 3199-3214)
authors_affiliation: Zora Zhiruo Wang, Akari Asai, Xinyan Velocity Yu, Frank F. Xu, Yiqing Xie, Graham Neubig, Daniel Fried. Primary affiliations: Carnegie Mellon University; University of Washington; University of Southern California. (Wang and Asai contributed equally.)
maintained_repo_url: https://code-rag-bench.github.io/ (project page; HuggingFace datasets/datastore at https://huggingface.co/code-rag-bench)
task_domain: code (retrieval-augmented code generation, RACG), spanning basic programming, open-domain coding, repository-level code generation/issue-solving, and code retrieval.
problem_setting: A holistic benchmark and empirical study of retrieval-augmented code generation. The setting is offline, single-turn, single-agent generation: a code LM is given a natural-language problem plus retrieved documents and produces a program evaluated by execution (pass@1). Two retrieval setups are studied: canonical retrieval (retrieve only from a manually annotated canonical datastore) and open retrieval (retrieve from any of five aggregated sources). Supervision exists in the form of manually annotated canonical/gold documents per task, enabling decoupled evaluation of retrieval quality (NDCG@10/Recall/Precision) separately from end-to-end generation quality. No model training is proposed; the work evaluates 10 off-the-shelf retrievers and 10 LMs.
what_is_retrieved: docs (Python library documentation), programming solutions (competition/canonical problem-solution pairs), online tutorials, StackOverflow posts, and GitHub repository files/code snippets. These serve as external contexts to augment code generation.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus. Retrieval targets a fixed, pre-built 25M-document datastore aggregated from five sources plus per-task canonical documents; there is no growing/episodic agent memory written at test time.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking objective. Retrieval is evaluated as a ranking task (NDCG@10 primary, plus Precision/Recall) against annotated canonical documents, and generation prepends a fixed number of top-k documents (top-5 default; top-1 from each source for mixed retrieval). It is not a completeness/minimal-set or precision-driven variable-size recommendation objective.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not a case-based reasoning system; if forced: Retrieve only, no Reuse-as-adaptation/Revise/Retain)
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work is framed as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG/RACG) and does not frame itself as case-based reasoning or cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner.
retrieval_unit: document / snippet. Concretely: a problem-solution document (NL problem concatenated with canonical solution) for programming-solutions; a library documentation entry; a StackOverflow post; an online tutorial page; a GitHub file or 20-line code snippet; and CodeSearchNet Python functions for the code-retrieval task. Documents are optionally chunked to 200-800 tokens (first 500 tokens used as default).
index_source: Static corpus, offline-constructed. A diverse open datastore aggregated offline from five sources (programming solutions, online tutorials, Python library docs, StackOverflow posts, GitHub files) totaling 25 million documents, plus manually annotated per-task canonical documents. The store is frozen, not online/test-time-induced.
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index (dense embeddings via sentence-transformers) and a sparse inverted index (BM25 via Pyserini). Documents are organized/separable by source pool (programming solutions, tutorials, docs, StackOverflow, GitHub), but retrieval is over flat per-source or aggregated indices; no dependency graph or hierarchical/cluster topology.
retriever_type: hybrid across the benchmark (the study evaluates sparse + dense + proprietary-API retrievers): sparse BM25; dense open models (BGE-base/large, GIST-base/large, SFR-Embedding-Mistral, Codesage-small, Jina-v2-code); proprietary APIs (voyage-code-2, openai-text-embedding-3-small). All are off-the-shelf; 10 retrievers total.
retriever_learning_signal: none (off-the-shelf). Retrievers are used as-is without task-specific training. Underlying models were pretrained with contrastive similarity objectives (e.g., MTEB-leaderboard dense models, code-specific contrastive models like Jina-v2-code/Codesage), but CodeRAG-Bench does not train or fine-tune any retriever on its tasks; it evaluates them with no learned downstream/RL signal.
query_construction: Raw input. The natural-language problem description (and, for repo-level tasks, the in-file context / issue) is used directly as the retrieval query against the datastore. No query decomposition, expansion, or intent extraction is introduced.
query_granularity: task-level (one-shot at t=0). A single query is formed per coding problem at the start; retrieval is not interleaved per reasoning step. (Exception: SWE-bench-Lite uses the Agentless n=21-way sampling + majority-vote localization pipeline for context, but the benchmark's core RACG protocol is one-shot task-level retrieval.)
when_to_retrieve: one-shot. Documents are retrieved once before generation and prepended to the prompt; there is no iterative or uncertainty-triggered retrieval in the core protocol.
retrieval_trigger_signal: fixed schedule (always retrieve once before generation). No token-confidence, attention/uncertainty, learned complexity classifier, reflection tokens, or agent-initiated trigger is used.
reranking: Yes, optionally. A cross-encoder reranking stage with BGE-reranker-base is applied on top-100 OpenAI-embedding results before generation, and as a post-retrieval chunk-reranking strategy. The paper reports that reranking within the optimal 200-800-token chunk range greatly degrades results, showing limited utility of current rerankers.
retrieved_context_refinement: Chunking/compression and optional rerank. Post-retrieval processing studied includes: (i) post-retrieval chunking (first N tokens of each document), (ii) post-retrieval reranking to find the most relevant N-token chunk (BGE-reranker-base), and (iii) pre-retrieval chunking (chunk then retrieve N-token pieces). Default uses first 500 tokens per document; chunking to 200-800 tokens is found best. No reason-in-documents distillation or learned distractor filtering.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (this is a code-document RAG benchmark, not a tool-retrieval setting). Documents are processed only by source-specific formatting (e.g., concatenating NL problem with solution for programming-solution docs) and chunking; no synthetic-query augmentation or instruction-tuned tool embeddings.
index_content_separation: N/A. No lightweight-index-then-content / progressive-disclosure separation is used; documents are chunked (default first 500 tokens) but there is no separated lightweight retrievable index over heavy on-demand content.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A. Static, offline-built datastore; no live-synchronized tool index, RapidAPI/RESTful/MCP/function-calling protocol, or CRUD auto-sync.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A. No inter-tool dependency modeling (this is document retrieval for code generation, not tool/API retrieval).
how_retrieved_used: prompt augmentation. Top-k retrieved documents (default top-5; top-1 per source for mixed retrieval) are prepended to the original coding problem in the LM context window; no training signal, latent-token injection, or explicit case adaptation.
planning_integration: one-shot exemplars/context at generation time (retrieve-then-generate). Retrieved documents are inserted into the prompt before the model generates the full program in a single pass; there is no per-step interleaving, MCTS/tree search, or hierarchical subtask planning in the core RACG protocol.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-answer. Retrieval happens once and conditions the single end-to-end code generation; it is not woven per-CoT-step, per-sentence/token, or per-tool-call.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not CBR). Retrieved documents are used verbatim as in-context augmentation; no case adaptation/revision mechanism.
retrieved_item_representation: raw document text injected into the prompt: raw problem-solution pairs, raw library-documentation entries, raw StackOverflow posts, raw tutorial text, and raw GitHub code snippets (optionally truncated/chunked to the first ~500 tokens). No distilled strategy/guideline, executable skill abstraction, or latent-soft tokens.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Mostly raw artifacts (raw code snippets, raw documentation, raw posts/tutorials, single problem-solution demonstrations). Programming-solution documents act as single demonstrations; library docs act as reference/hint material. No distilled strategy or procedural-skill abstraction.
noise_robustness_mechanism: None built-in. The study explicitly analyzes (does not fix) noise: it shows models are easily distracted by irrelevant/distracting retrieved contexts and that adding more low-ranked documents introduces noise and degrades generation. No retriever-aware training, relevance evaluator, self-reflection, or distractor-aware SFT is proposed; robustness is left as an identified open challenge.
memory_type: none. The system uses a static external datastore, not an episodic/skill-library/workflow/procedural/graph/latent memory that the agent writes to.
write_back: False. No new experiences/cases/skills are stored back into the datastore; the store is fixed offline.
online_growth: False. The retrievable store is frozen after offline construction; it does not grow during deployment/test-time.
write_back_trigger: never. No write-back events occur (no success/failure/per-step/reflective/human-validated writes).
failure_experience_usage: N/A / none. No storage or retrieval of failed/negative experiences; failure cases are only analyzed qualitatively (e.g., distraction by irrelevant contexts, over-complicated generations) but not written to any memory.
memory_evolution_update: N/A / none. No stored entries are mutated (no append-only/dedup-merge/delta-update/refine-overwrite/forget-prune/link-and-evolve); the datastore is static.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: False. Retrieval/document-selection is fixed similarity top-k (or BM25 ranking), not a learned/RL-optimized policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: N/A / none. Single-pass, single-generator evaluation with a shared static datastore; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory/experience sharing.
benchmarks: HumanEval (164), MBPP (500), LiveCodeBench (400; generation-only, no gold docs), DS-1000 (1000), ODEX (945) plus an ODEX-hard subset (20 least-common libraries), RepoEval function split (373), SWE-bench-Lite (300), and CodeSearchNet-Python (CSN, 22,177; code-retrieval task). Retrieval datastore: 25 million documents from five sources (programming solutions, online tutorials ~79.4k, Python library docs, StackOverflow posts ~23.5M, GitHub files).
benchmark_family: code. Spans code generation (basic: HumanEval/MBPP/LiveCodeBench; open-domain: DS-1000/ODEX; repository-level: RepoEval, SWE-bench-Lite) and code retrieval (CodeSearchNet-Py). SWE-bench and RepoEval are code/repo-level benchmarks; CodeSearchNet is the code-retrieval benchmark.
baselines: Retrievers (10): BM25; GIST-base/large; BGE-base/large; SFR-Embedding-Mistral; Codesage-small; Jina-v2-code; OpenAI-text-embedding-3-small; voyage-code-2; plus BGE-reranker-base reranking. Generators (10): StarCoder2-7B, CodeGemma-7B, CodeLlama-7B/34B, DeepSeekCoder-7B/33B, Llama3, Command-R, GPT-3.5-turbo-0125, GPT-4o (also GPT-4, Claude-3-haiku/sonnet, Gemini-1.5-flash/pro in appendix). Reference conditions: no-context (w/o), gold/canonical documents, and RACG (retrieved) settings.
key_metrics: Retrieval: NDCG@10 (primary), plus Precision and Recall. Generation: pass@1 via execution-based evaluation (functional correctness; SWE-bench resolve rate). Retrieval efficiency: indexing/search latency and index storage size.
headline_result: Retrieving high-quality (canonical/gold) contexts yields notable RACG gains, e.g., GPT-4o improves by 27.4% (absolute, resolve rate) on SWE-bench-Lite and 6.9% on the harder ODEX subset when given canonical documents; some RACG settings even surpass the gold-document setting. However, current retrievers struggle to fetch useful contexts (especially with low lexical overlap, e.g., DS-1000/ODEX NDCG@10 as low as ~5-37), and weaker/long-context generators improve less, revealing substantial room for improvement.
ablations: (1) Retriever comparison (Table 3): dense models frequently surpass BM25; code-specific retrievers (Jina-v2-code, voyage-code-2) outperform comparable general models (Jina-v2-code beats GIST-base/BGE-base by 7.4/6.6 avg NDCG@10); larger models help (GIST-large > GIST-base, SFR-Mistral 7B strong). (2) Retrieval efficiency vs accuracy (Table 4): BM25 is orders of magnitude cheaper; SFR-Mistral needs >5x index storage and ~100x encode latency. (3) Number of documents (Appendix E): top-5 is the sweet spot across context-length budgets; more docs add noise. (4) Chunking strategy (Fig 2/Table 9): 200-800-token chunks are best; reranking within that range degrades results. (5) Source comparison (Table 7): StackOverflow/tutorials help HumanEval; programming solutions most help ODEX. (6) ODEX-hard (least-common libraries): documentation augmentation improves 20.3-40.1%, verifying RACG helps for less-popular libraries. (7) Does RACG help stronger models (Appendix F): mixed results; models often distracted by non-canonical contexts.
evaluation_decoupling: Yes. Intrinsic retrieval metrics (NDCG@10/Precision/Recall) are reported separately (Table 3) from end-to-end execution-based generation metrics (pass@1, Tables 5-7), and the benchmark explicitly provides reproducible evaluation of both retrieval and end-to-end generation.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both, in a decoupled way: an intermediate process metric (retrieval quality, NDCG@10) is reported alongside the final outcome metric (execution-based pass@1 / resolve rate). It does not score reasoning faithfulness or step-wise trajectory quality (single-pass generation).
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Reported (Table 4). On sampled CodeSearchNet-Python (10k queries, 100k docs), BM25 indexing/search takes only seconds (0.15ms/0.02ms per query, 141MB); GIST-base 3.7ms/9.7ms encode/search, 440MB+307MB; SFR-Mistral 316ms/113ms, 14220MB index (>5x storage, ~100x encode latency vs GIST-base), 1638MB model; Voyage-code/OpenAI-03 ~22-47ms with ~1172MB. The paper argues retrieval efficiency must be weighed against accuracy in RAG pipelines.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k with budget-capped chunking. Default prepends top-5 retrieved documents (top-1 per source for 5-source mixed retrieval), each truncated to the first 500 tokens (optimal per ablation), to fit all model context limits. Number-of-documents ablation (top-1/2/5/10) finds 5 best; chunk-size ablation finds 200-800 tokens best.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (benchmark/empirical study, not a survey). Organizing axes of the benchmark: four task categories (basic programming, open-domain, repository-level, code retrieval) x two retrieval setups (canonical vs open) x five datastore sources; evaluation across 10 retrievers and 10 LMs. References: 52.
benchmark_construction_and_size: 9k coding tasks across 6-8 datasets and a 25M-document retrieval datastore (StackOverflow ~23.5M posts, online tutorials ~79.4k, plus library docs/programming solutions/GitHub). Construction: aggregates existing datasets (HumanEval, MBPP, LiveCodeBench, DS-1000, ODEX, RepoEval, SWE-bench-Lite, CodeSearchNet) and manually annotates canonical documents per task (e.g., avg 1.4/1.2 doc entries for DS-1000/ODEX; 20-line snippets for RepoEval; gold edited files for SWE-bench). Answers are execution-verifiable (test-case execution; NDCG@10 for retrieval). Difficulty signal: SWE-bench-Lite remains very hard (only GPT-3.5-turbo and GPT-4o achieve non-trivial results; GPT-4o ~2.3% w/o, ~30.7% with gold docs).
builds_on: Aggregates and extends existing code-generation datasets (HumanEval, MBPP, LiveCodeBench, DS-1000, ODEX, RepoEval, SWE-bench-Lite, CodeSearchNet) and RAG/retrieval infrastructure (Pyserini/BM25, sentence-transformers, MTEB-leaderboard dense retrievers, code retrievers Jina-v2-code/Codesage, voyage-code-2, OpenAI embeddings). For SWE-bench it uses the Agentless localization pipeline (Xia et al., 2024). Conceptually builds on text-RAG benchmarks BEIR and KILT.
contrasts_with: Positioned against prior RACG work that relied largely on BM25 alone (e.g., DocPrompting/Zhou et al. 2023, SWE-bench/Jimenez et al. 2024) without comprehensive multi-retriever comparison, and against text-centric RAG benchmarks (BEIR, KILT) that do not cover code; contrasts the assumption that neural retrievers underperform BM25 out-of-domain by showing dense retrievers frequently surpass BM25 on code.
lineage: Group B (retrieval-augmented task solving) - belongs to the benchmark/evaluation lineage of retrieval-augmented code generation; a holistic RACG testbed providing decoupled retrieval + end-to-end evaluation, intended to standardize and advance code-oriented RAG methods (Surveys/Benchmarks branch).
